{
  "score": 6.5,
  "flaws": [
    "In the close-up view (image 2), the lowest wooden crossbeam support on the right side is detached and hanging in mid-air next to the short dark pillar instead of resting on top of it.",
    "The blue catch box around the target cup at the end of the track looks like a messy collage of overlapping primitives—there is a red block, a brass ring, and a tiny vertical gold sliver clipping straight through the side wall.",
    "In the top-down view (image 4), the base plate and the highest support pillars at the top-left start of the run hang past the back edge of the desk over empty space.",
    "The marble run design is mechanically boring: it is just one long, uninterrupted straight orange chute from start to finish rather than an engaging multi-stage desk toy.",
    "The horizontal crossbars under the ramp are plain, unchamfered rectangular blocks that clip into the vertical pillars rather than sitting cleanly in brackets or joints."
  ],
  "summary": "The marble run achieves 16/16 reliability and has nice desk props, but it is just a single straight ramp with significant geometry errors: floating/misaligned support crossbeams, clipping primitives on the catch box, and the base overhanging the back edge of the desk."
}
